# ato-mcp — full site content for LLMs

> The Australian tax knowledge base for AI agents: an MCP (Model Context Protocol)
> service giving cited retrieval over 34,500+ ATO documents, the income tax and
> GST Acts and 4,900+ public rulings, plus a personal-facts layer and four
> deterministic tax workflow tools. Hosted-only: point any MCP client at
> https://api.ato-mcp.com.au/mcp and sign in with your browser.
> Not tax advice: every tool returns structured data plus resolvable ATO
> citations for an agent to reason over.

Canonical site: https://ato-mcp.com.au · Short index: https://ato-mcp.com.au/llms.txt

## What ato-mcp is

ato-mcp is an MCP server for Australian tax. It plugs into Claude, ChatGPT, Codex,
Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code or any Model Context Protocol host and turns the
Australian tax corpus into 13 tools an AI agent can call. Every answer is cited
back to its source (ato.gov.au guidance, legislation, or an ATO public ruling).

The corpus, in numbers:

- 34,564 documents and 286,638 searchable passages
- ato.gov.au guidance pages, the ITAA 1997, the ITAA 1936 and the GST Act
  (6,468 sections of tax law plus 2,310 statutory definitions, including the
  GST Act's s 195-1 dictionary)
- 4,937 public rulings across ten series (TR, TD, GSTR, PCG and more), with
  withdrawn rulings clearly flagged
- 64,217 citation links tying rulings, guidance and legislation into one graph
- Rebuilt on a monthly cycle from ato.gov.au, the Federal Register of
  Legislation and law.ato.gov.au, and served fresh

## Install (https://ato-mcp.com.au/install)

One line, then sign in with your browser — your account is created on first
sign-in, no token to copy.

- Remote MCP endpoint: https://api.ato-mcp.com.au/mcp (streamable HTTP, OAuth)
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http ato https://api.ato-mcp.com.au/mcp`
- Cursor / VS Code / Codex / Gemini CLI / Claude.ai / ChatGPT: add the same
  remote endpoint as an HTTP MCP server in the client's MCP settings — the
  install picker at https://ato-mcp.com.au/install has the exact command or
  config snippet per client
- Stdio-only clients: the open-source npm package proxies the hosted server —
  `npx -y ato-mcp` (Node 22+); first run opens your browser to sign in

## The 13 tools (https://ato-mcp.com.au/docs)

Retrieval:

- `search` — hybrid keyword + semantic search over the whole corpus, rank-fused,
  point-in-time aware. Example: `search({ query: "instant asset write-off eligibility", k: 5 })`
- `get_chunks` — resolve chunk_ids to full passages with optional neighbouring
  context. Example: `get_chunks({ chunk_ids: ["legis:…/8-1#0"], neighbours: 1 })`
- `get_doc` — fetch a whole document: metadata, full text in reading order, and
  its anchor list. Example: `get_doc({ doc_id: "legis:c2004a05138/8-1" })`
- `get_doc_anchors` — the citation graph around a document: anchors, inbound and
  outbound references. Example: `get_doc_anchors({ doc_id: "legis:c2004a05138/8-1" })`
- `get_definition` — statutory definitions (ITAA 1997 Dictionary and friends),
  point-in-time selectable. Example: `get_definition({ term: "depreciating asset" })`
- `get_threshold` — time-keyed scalar facts: instant asset write-off limit, GST
  registration threshold, CGT discount, super caps and more.
  Example: `get_threshold({ name: "instant_asset_write_off" })`
- `fetch` — live-fetch a page by URI scheme (ato:, ato-law:, legis:) when
  freshness matters. Example: `fetch({ uri: "ato:tax-rates-and-codes/…" })`
- `stats` — corpus snapshot: counts and schema version.

Personal context:

- `get_user_facts` — the user's onboarded tax profile (about 25 fields: business
  structure, GST registration, residency and so on) that the agent reads once
  per session instead of re-asking.

Workflows (deterministic, cited, branch on the user's taxpayer structure):

- `deduction_discovery` — every plausibly-applicable deduction category for the
  user's taxpayer shape, cited and confidence-rated.
- `depreciation_helper` — prime-cost / diminishing-value / instant-asset-write-off /
  pool / Division 43 schedules, computed deterministically.
- `bas_prep_checklist` — a tiered, cited BAS checklist for the user's reporting
  period: labels, evidence, gotchas.
- `audit_risk_check` — heuristic ATO red-flags over a draft return, risk-banded
  with the guidance behind each flag.

Full tool reference (schemas, examples, errors):
https://github.com/william-laverty/ato-mcp/blob/main/docs/tools.md

## FAQ

**Is this tax advice?**
No. ato-mcp retrieves published ATO material and runs fixed calculations, always
with the source attached. Confidence ratings and risk bands are guides, not
professional judgement. Your agent does the reasoning, and decisions that matter
should still go past a registered tax agent.

**What does ato-mcp store about me?**
Your onboarding facts (business structure, GST registration and so on — about 25
fields you control), your sign-in identity, and basic usage counts. Never tool
names, never query content, never results: the database physically has nowhere
to store them, and the privacy page is generated from that same schema so it
can't drift.

**Which agents does it work with?**
Anything that speaks the Model Context Protocol: Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini
CLI, Cursor, VS Code and more. One line to install, then sign in with your
browser.

**How current is the corpus?**
The corpus is rebuilt from ato.gov.au, the Federal Register of Legislation and
law.ato.gov.au on a monthly cycle and served fresh. The stats tool reports the
live snapshot.

**Is it open source?**
Most clients connect directly to the hosted endpoint with no local code at all.
The optional npm client is open source (AGPL-3.0) and public, so you can verify
exactly what it does. The hosted retrieval platform and the corpus are
maintained privately.

**Is there an MCP server for Australian tax?**
Yes. ato-mcp is an MCP server for Australian tax: it gives any agent that
speaks the Model Context Protocol (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor,
VS Code) cited retrieval over 34,500+ ATO documents, the income tax and GST
Acts and 4,900+ public rulings.

**What is MCP (the Model Context Protocol)?**
MCP is the open standard AI agents use to call outside tools and data sources.
ato-mcp uses it to hand your agent 13 Australian tax tools: search over the
corpus, statutory definitions, current rates and thresholds, and four workflow
tools, with every answer carrying its ATO citation.

**Do I need to be a developer?**
No. If you can paste a command and sign in with your browser, you can connect
ato-mcp. The install page (https://ato-mcp.com.au/install) walks through each
client step by step.

Full FAQ: https://ato-mcp.com.au/faq

## Compared with the alternatives (https://ato-mcp.com.au/compare)

Browsing ato.gov.au yourself: the answers exist but span thousands of pages,
rulings and thresholds; one real question often takes an hour or more.
Asking a chatbot on its own: fast but uncited, drawn from training data of
uncertain age; thresholds go stale silently and you can't act on "probably".
Your agent with ato-mcp: the same agent, grounded in the actual corpus, aware
of your saved tax profile, running deterministic calculations, with the ATO
source attached to every claim.

## About (https://ato-mcp.com.au/about)

ato-mcp is designed, built and run by William Laverty, an Australian software
developer (https://github.com/william-laverty). It is a small, independent
product: no invented testimonials, no made-up user counts, and the client code
is public so you can check both. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or
operated by the Australian Taxation Office. Contact: GitHub issues for product
questions, privacy@ato-mcp.com.au for privacy and data requests.

## Latest update (2026-07-04): The new ato-mcp

https://ato-mcp.com.au/blogs/the-new-ato-mcp

The biggest release yet: sign in with your browser (the token flow is gone), a
personal tax-facts layer so your agent understands your situation, and a rebuilt
corpus — 34,564 documents (up from ~29,900), 286,638 passages (+37% in one
release), rulings coverage more than doubled to 4,937, the ITAA 1936 and GST Act
added alongside the ITAA 1997, and 64,217 citation links tying it all together,
with measurably better search.
